addon_desc_knip: Finds unused files, exports, dependencies, and catalog entries
addon_desc_ultracite: Lint and formatting presets with framework rules and AI code quality checks
desc_better_auth: Email and password sign-in, with sessions in the database
desc_drizzle: Drizzle ORM v1 with SQL migrations
desc_electron: Desktop app around the web app, packaged with electron-builder
desc_hono: Standalone API server built on Hono
desc_next: Full-stack React with the App Router and React Compiler
desc_openapi: REST API with @hono/zod-openapi and a typed client
desc_orpc: End-to-end type-safe RPC with OpenAPI docs
desc_postgres: PostgreSQL server, run by Docker Compose in development
desc_self: API routes served by the frontend framework, beside its pages
desc_shadcn: Base UI components in a shared UI package
desc_spa: Client-rendered React app built with Vite
desc_tanstack_start: Full-stack React with SSR, server routes, and server functions
desc_vite_plus: Unified toolchain for dev, build, test, lint, and format
desc_playwright: Control actions and assertions in code, wait automatically for elements, and inspect each step in a trace. Fits clear acceptance criteria and regression suites maintained over time.
document_description: Pick your stack, run one command, and get a modern full-stack TypeScript project. Built on Vite+, with engineering rules your AI can read; every combination is verified end to end.
extensions_about: Choose the capabilities you need. Select several without changing the existing test flow.
fit_better_auth: For apps where users have accounts.
fit_docker: For your own server or any container host.
fit_electron: For the same web app in its own window, packaged as an installer.
fit_hono: For an API that mobile apps or other services share.
fit_next: For SEO-focused sites, on the most popular React framework.
fit_none_auth: For public sites with no sign-in.
fit_none_backend: For static sites with no data.
fit_none_desktop: For an app that runs in the browser only.
fit_none_framework: For an API that apps or scripts call.
fit_openapi: For a standard REST API that others call.
fit_orpc: For an API only your own frontend calls.
fit_postgres: For production apps with many users.
fit_self: For one app to build and deploy. The simplest setup.
fit_spa: For dashboards and tools behind a sign-in.
fit_sqlite: For prototypes and single-server apps. Nothing to install.
fit_tanstack_start: For sites that need SEO or fast first loads.
home_base_body: Generated projects include type checking, code conventions, and behavioral tests. Developers and AI tools can use the same checks to verify a change.
home_body: Pick your stack, run one command, and get a modern full-stack TypeScript project. Built on Vite+, with engineering rules your AI can read. All {stacks} combinations are verified end to end.
home_cta_body: Pick each layer, let the rest adapt, and start with one command.
home_verify_body: Every stack is installed, checked, tested and built from scratch. The output that passed keeps a fingerprint, so you can check what you get.
home_verify_follow: Verification for the stack selected above
knip_scope_default: Discovers pnpm workspaces, package entries, and tool configuration automatically, with no extra config file. When selected, ready checks for unused code and dependencies.
knip_scope_desktop: knip.json declares Electron main, preload, and both Vite build configurations as entries. Other workspaces are discovered automatically.
not_found_body: The address may have moved, or it never existed.
not_found_title: This page isn’t on the map.
not_verified: Not yet verified at this version
note_any_postgres: or point DATABASE_URL at any Postgres
pillar_quality_body: Strict static analysis and consistent formatting surface problems while you code. AGENTS.md documents the project conventions, so developers and AI follow the same rules.
pillar_tests_body: Tests target real behavior, not coverage numbers: integration tests use two accounts to verify authorization, and browser tests cover sign-up, sign-in, and data operations. Scope follows the selected capabilities.
pillar_types_body: oRPC carries API types to callers. When a response field changes, type checking identifies code that still uses the old field.
project_name_invalid: Project name "{name}" must start with a lowercase letter, contain only lowercase letters, digits, and dashes, and be at most {max} characters
role_api_about: How the frontend calls the backend.
role_api_none: Only a health check. Routes are yours to write.
role_api_question: How does the frontend talk to the backend?
role_auth_none: No sign-in. Every visitor sees the same app.
role_backend_about: Server code that handles requests, data, and secrets.
role_backend_none: No server code. The frontend ships as static files.
role_database_about: Keeps data such as users and orders.
role_deployment_about: How the app is packaged for a server.
role_deployment_none: No image. Runs anywhere Node.js runs.
role_desktop_about: The web app in its own window, packaged as an installer.
role_desktop_none: No installer. The app runs in the browser.
role_desktop_question: Does it need a desktop app?
role_framework_about: The pages users open in a browser.
role_framework_none: No pages. Only an API for other apps to call.
toolchain_scope: Development, production builds, formatting, linting, and type checks share one configuration and command set.
ultracite_scope: Adds Ultracite lint and formatting presets to vp check, with framework rules for the selected stack. Opting out keeps Vite+ baseline checks, type checking, and the existing test flow.
verified_passed: {#code}vp run ready{/code} passed on this exact output
viz_all_passed: vp run ready: every check passed
viz_render_caption: Client and server rendering load content and enable interaction at different stages.
viz_render_status: Sequence and timing are illustrative; actual behavior depends on the application and environment.
viz_tests_caption: Two test suites for the same todo app. Plant a real bug, a list that shows every user's todos, and run both.
viz_tests_caption_broken: Thirty-six tests stay green while every user can read everyone's todos. Two of seven fail and point to the leak.
viz_tests_caught: vibestart suite: {count} tests fail and point to the leak
viz_tests_shipped: Typical suite: all green, and the leak ships
viz_tests_typical: What an AI writes when asked for tests
runtime_about: Runs the Hono server. The package manager, web framework and test tools are independent.
fit_bun: Use Bun to run Hono, with TypeScript and environment files built in.
fit_node: Keep the current Node.js runtime for Hono.
desc_bun: Bun runtime for the Hono server; web frameworks and tools stay on Node.js
change_demo_label: Example project · Hono + oRPC + Better Auth
change_types_draft: The API now returns name, but the page still reads title.
change_types_check: Type checking reports the field that no longer exists.
change_types_fix: The page reads name, matching the API response.
change_quality_draft: A todo submission refreshes the list without handling the returned promise.
change_quality_check: Lint reports an unhandled promise that must be awaited or have a rejection handler.
change_quality_fix: Await the refresh so the caller can handle a failure.
change_tests_draft: The list query omits the user filter and can return another account’s todos.
change_tests_check: After Alice creates a todo, Bob’s list should be empty. The integration test detects another account’s data.
change_tests_fix: Filtering by the current user keeps the two accounts’ data separate.
create_agent_prompt:
Create a project with vibestart. Install its skill first:
{skill}

Then follow it to choose a stack that fits my needs and create the project.

My needs:
create_agent_title: Let an AI agent choose the stack
create_agent_about: Copy the prompt into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc., then add what you want to build. The agent picks the stack and creates the project.
desc_e2e: Mix natural-language goals with scripted assertions. An AI agent explores the UI, and verified actions can replay from cache. Fits evolving interfaces and teams adding user-journey coverage quickly.
testing_about: End-to-end tests follow complete user journeys, such as signing in or checking out, to check that the UI and backend work together.
tests_scope_unit: Every stack runs its unit tests on Vitest, beside the code.
tests_scope_integration: Every stack runs its unit tests on Vitest. This one also runs API integration tests against a real database.
tests_scope_e2e_none: An API-only project has no web app, so it has no end-to-end tests.
